evidence: The only shipped data file is environment/assets/seed_data.json (identical bytes in solution/app/seed/, sha256 b256f85e58dde8370cd3577123f785daf6988f4d00506533f19485279dca7bf8, matching raw-evidence-index.json); it parses, and a python -B integrity script confirmed 18 unique message ids, every author/client/walled email resolves to one of the 5 accounts, every timer_days is in timer_options_days [null,1,7,30], every message 'at' <= clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z, all 5 parent links (K-14->K-1, K-15->K-14, K-4->K-3, K-12->K-6, K-9->K-8) resolve within the same matter to an earlier message, and all 13 read_up_to pointers resolve to a message in the named matter; no read pointer exists for walled Dev on M-12 or for clients on matters not theirs. Seed agrees with the public notes and criteria: accounts/names/roles match walls-and-retention.md table, Dev walled from M-12 (walls-and-retention.md:68), K-10 exactly 7 days old vs K-11 one second younger (functional judge.toml:127), K-1 expired with surviving held reply chain K-14/K-15 (judge.toml:120, deliberate placeholder case per walls-and-retention.md:78), K-18 3 May / K-13 4 May with version '2,400' (judge.toml:138-139), held edited K-2 with version 'Landlords notice recieved.' (judge.toml:253,259). Data is synthetic: .test reserved domain emails, fictional names/firm, no DOB/addresses/phones; no password, token or secret inside the seed (password123 is only in the /instructions notes, the expected demo-credential profile). Free text has no script, event handler, javascript: URL or judge-directed prompt injection (grep negative); K-16's 'Schedule 2 ... clause 4 ... rent' is benign markup deliberately required by conversations.md:22 to display literally and graded at judge.toml:192, not an exploit payload. Counterexample attempts: (a) a seed-consistency-related broken app could not pass by exploiting the data since no orphan rows or self-contradictions exist to lean on; (b) a conforming alternative ordering unread positions by numeric id instead of sent time would differ (K-ids are not time-monotonic, e.g. K-17 sent 3 May before K-10), but the brief defines order by send time, the golden imports by 'at', and no criterion asserts a seeded unread count other than Gwen's 'at least 2' after three new posts, so no conforming app is mis-graded. Scope note: this is a static data review; whether the golden runtime imports the seed correctly is covered by scripted golden evidence elsewhere, not re-run here.
